https://english.news.cn/europe/20260724/.text: Romania shoots down drone breaching airspace BUCHAREST, July 24 (Xinhua) -- Romanian President Nicusor Dan said Friday that Romania shot down a drone breaching its airspace in the Buzau County. He said that the authorities are conducting investigations at the scene of the incident to establish all the circumstances in which the drone entered Romania's airspace and to identify it. "It is important to note that the area was uninhabited, which is why the pilot was able to fire from above," Dan added. Romania's Ministry of National Defense said in a press release that its radar surveillance system detected an aerial target approximately 20 km east of Sulina. The track subsequently penetrated the national airspace. An F-16 fighter aircraft of the Romanian Air Force engaged the target with an air-to-air missile and neutralized it over an unpopulated area in the vicinity of Padina, Buzau County. ■ News In-depth Sports Business Culture World China Regions Asia & Pacific Europe Middle East North America South America Africa Organizations Services Weather Live & Work in China Doing Business Investment Visit China Study in China More Special Reports Photos Video Corrections About Us Contact Us Media Qiushi Journal Taiwan.cn Youth.cn GMW.cn CE.cn Ecns.cn China Daily CRI.cn China.org.cn People's Daily

https://www.dw.com/en/us-pulls-bombers-o.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5NkR9 US B-1 bombers stationed at RAF Fairford were used for strikes against Iran Image: Alastair Grant/AP Photo/picture alliance Advertisement A week after several men were detained at the Royal Air Force (RAF) base in the UK's Fairford on suspicion of planning terrorist attacks, a Pentagon official announced that the United States had removed its B-1 bombers from the base northwest of London. On Sunday, aircraft monitoring sites showed the B-1 aircraft flying out of the UK base. "While operational security precluded us from ​confirming the movement of our assets and forces ​in real-time, ‌we can acknowledge now that all US bombers that were deployed to RAF Fairford have re-deployed to their home ‌stations in the United States," a Pentagon spokesman wrote ‌in ​a statement. A dozen B-1 bombers had been stationed at RAF Fairford, the British airbase used by the US. London previously allowed the Pentagon to fly sorties out of Fairford against Iranian missile sites which were threatening ships in the Strait of Hormuz.
